title: Irrationality Measure Controls Long-Wavelength Charge Fluctuations in Quasiperiodic Systems
abstract: Quasiperiodic order is characterized by irrational frequencies whose rational approximability known as irrationality measure defines distinct arithmetic classes. We establish that this arithmetic classification has direct physical consequences for long-wavelength charge fluctuations. In translation-covariant quasiperiodic systems, the infrared scaling of charge fluctuation is governed by the interplay between the irrationality exponent of irrational frequency and the large-harmonic decay of the hull charge profile: the latter determines the available charge weight, while the former controls how efficiently that weight is transferred to the infrared. Consequently, all algebraic irrational frequencies share the same arithmetic scaling, whereas exceptionally well-approximable transcendental frequencies can exhibit strongly enhanced infrared fluctuation scaling. We further prove that occupied states separated from the Fermi level by a gap stable throughout the hull contribute only an analytic infrared background, leaving the nontrivial scaling to near-Fermi states. Our results extend to general translation-covariant multi-frequency quasiperiodic systems.
summary: This work establishes that the long-wavelength charge fluctuations in quasiperiodic systems are fundamentally controlled by the arithmetic properties of the irrational modulation frequency $ eta$. It derives a scaling law linking the fluctuation exponent to both the frequency's irrationality measure and the smoothness of the system's charge profile. This provides a deep theoretical link between number theory and condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The paper determines the fundamental principle governing long-wavelength charge fluctuations in quasiperiodic systems, linking it directly to the arithmetic properties of the irrational modulation frequency.
main_result: The scaling of infrared charge fluctuations is governed by a relationship involving the system's regularity exponent ($r$) and the irrationality measure ($\mu( eta)$) of the frequency, specifically $\alpha + 1 = 2r / (\mu( eta) - 1)$.
method: The analysis uses Fourier decomposition and scaling arguments to relate the integrated low-momentum weight (charge fluctuations) to the arithmetic properties of the quasiperiodicity.
model_or_system: The study focuses on translation-covariant quasiperiodic systems, exemplified by the Aubry-André model, described by Hamiltonians $H(	heta)$ modulated by an irrational frequency $ eta$.
key_observables: Charge fluctuation variance $\sigma^2(R)$, integrated infrared weight $Z(K)$, and the hyperuniformity class $\alpha$.
important_parameters: Irrationality measure $\mu( eta)$, regularity exponent $r$, and the modulation frequency $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the relevant hull Fourier amplitudes obey an algebraic decay bound $|c_m| \lesssim |m|^{-r}$ and that the spectral gap is stable for the deep sector contribution to be negligible.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the charge distribution and the running average of the charge variance $\sigma_2(R)$ for different irrational frequencies ($\phi$ vs. another irrational).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical link between arithmetic properties ($\mu( eta)$) and physical observables (charge fluctuations), deriving the central scaling relation by analyzing the contributions from near-Fermi states versus the deep spectral gap.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between number theory (irrationality measure) and physical transport/fluctuation properties in quasiperiodic lattices provides a powerful, non-trivial diagnostic tool for characterizing the underlying order.
